attempts.title: lookup_customer parameter name mismatch: tool spec says 'email' but function expects 'customer_email'

hypothesis.title: lookup_customer parameter name mismatch: tool spec says 'email' but function expects 'customer_email'
hypothesis.root_cause: The TOOL_SPECS definition declares the parameter as 'email', so the LLM calls lookup_customer({"email": "..."}) — but the actual Python function signature is `def lookup_customer(customer_email: str)`. When run_tool unpacks the JSON args dict with **args, it passes `email=...` which doesn't match `customer_email`, causing TypeError every time. This means customer data is never retrieved, so the agent has no plan/tier context to apply the priority policy correctly, and the KB search also fails because the agent's queries don't match article titles/tags (search_kb does substring matching on title and tags, but the queries sent are too verbose or don't match the stored tags).
evidence: task `password` step 2: lookup_customer returned 'ERROR: TypeError: lookup_customer() got an unexpected keyword argument 'email'' (all 6 tasks)
task `webhooks-pro` step 2: same error, tool_errors=1
task `double-charge` step 2 and 3: same error, tool_errors=2
task `past-due` step 2 and 3: same error, tool_errors=2
triage/tools.py:40: def lookup_customer(customer_email: str) — parameter is 'customer_email'
triage/tools.py:17: TOOL_SPECS declares parameter name as 'email'
All 6 tasks fail correct_kb_article; search_kb returns '[]' every time because queries like 'reset password locked out account' don't substring-match article titles or tags
hypothesis.fix_plan:
1. In triage/tools.py, rename the function parameter from `customer_email` to `email` so it matches what the LLM passes: `def lookup_customer(email: str) -> dict:` and update the body to use `email` instead of `customer_email`.
2. The KB search returning empty results is because search_kb checks `q in a['tags']` where tags is likely a list not a string — verify and fix the tag matching (change to `any(q in tag.lower() for tag in a['tags'])` if tags is a list, or keep as-is if it's a string). Also improve the SYSTEM prompt to instruct the agent to use short, keyword-focused KB queries matching article titles, and include the priority policy from policy.py so the model applies P1/P2/P3 correctly without needing customer plan data.
3. Update SYSTEM prompt to embed the PRIORITY_POLICY from policy.py so the model knows P1 is only for enterprise production outages, P2 for pro production outages or enterprise issues, and P3 for everything else.
hypothesis.expected_effect: Fixing the parameter name mismatch will eliminate all 11 tool_errors and allow customer plan/tier to be retrieved, enabling correct priority assignment. Combined with the prompt fix for priority policy, correct_priority should flip for password (P3), double-charge (P3), webhooks-pro (P2). Fixing KB search (tag matching + better query guidance) should flip correct_kb_article for all 6 tasks. Expected: all 6 tasks pass all checks.

attempts.title: System prompt priority policy missing past_due P2 rule causing past-due task to get P3

hypothesis.title: System prompt priority policy missing past_due P2 rule causing past-due task to get P3
hypothesis.root_cause: The SYSTEM prompt defines P2 only for pro plan production issues and enterprise non-outage issues. It omits the policy.py rule that a past_due account that cannot pay is also P2. The agent therefore assigns P3 to the past-due billing case.
evidence: task past-due: priority='P3' expected 'P2'
policy.py PRIORITY_POLICY states P2 includes 'a past_due account that cannot pay'
prompts.py SYSTEM P2 bullet has no mention of past_due accounts
hypothesis.fix_plan: Update the P2 bullet in SYSTEM to add the past_due rule: change 'P2: pro plan customer AND production issue, OR enterprise plan customer with non-outage issue.' to 'P2: pro plan customer AND production issue, OR enterprise plan customer with non-outage issue, OR any customer whose account status is past_due and cannot pay.'
hypothesis.expected_effect: Fixes correct_priority for task past-due. One additional check passes.

attempts.title: search_kb does full-string substring match so multi-word queries never match individual title/tag words

hypothesis.title: search_kb does full-string substring match so multi-word queries never match individual title/tag words
hypothesis.root_cause: The search_kb function checks if the entire lowercased query string (e.g. 'webhook delivery failure') is a substring of the article title or tags. KB article titles and tags likely contain individual words like 'webhook' but not the full phrase, so every search returns []. Fix: split the query into tokens and match if ANY token appears in the title or any tag. Also fix the system prompt priority policy to match policy.py (add past_due P2 rule and clarify enterprise non-outage is P2).
evidence: webhooks-pro step 2: search_kb query 'webhook delivery failure' returned '[]'
webhooks-pro step 3: search_kb query 'webhook troubleshooting' returned '[]'
outage-enterprise step 1: search_kb query 'API 500 errors' returned '[]'
double-charge step 1: search_kb query 'billing refund duplicate' returned '[]'
double-charge step 2: search_kb query 'duplicate charge refund' returned '[]'
past-due step 2: search_kb query 'expired card payment' returned '[]'
past-due step 3: search_kb query 'billing payment method' returned '[]'
All failing tasks have kb_article='' because every search_kb call returns empty list
hypothesis.fix_plan: In tools.py search_kb: split query into individual tokens and match an article if ANY token appears in the lowercased title or in ANY lowercased tag. In prompts.py: update priority policy to match policy.py exactly, adding 'past_due account that cannot pay is P2' and ensuring enterprise non-outage issues are P2 (fixes seats-enterprise and past-due priority).
hypothesis.expected_effect: Fixes correct_kb_article for outage-enterprise (KB-301), webhooks-pro (KB-302), double-charge (KB-202), past-due (KB-203), seats-enterprise (KB-401). Fixes correct_priority for past-due (P2) and seats-enterprise (P2). All 6 tasks should pass.

attempts.summary: Fix search_kb to match any query token against article title/tags instead of full-string substring match

attempts.title: System prompt priority policy missing past_due P2 rule

hypothesis.title: System prompt priority policy missing past_due P2 rule
hypothesis.root_cause: The SYSTEM prompt in triage/prompts.py does not include the rule that a past_due account that cannot pay should be P2. The policy.py (source of truth) explicitly states 'P2: ... or a past_due account that cannot pay.' but the SYSTEM prompt only says 'P3: everything else (starter/free plans, billing questions, account issues, non-production problems).' The round 2 attempt added this rule but also changed the wording in a way that may have confused the model ('OR any customer whose account status is past_due and cannot pay' is redundant/awkward). The fix needs to be cleaner and more direct, matching the exact policy.py wording.
evidence: task past-due step 2: priority='P3', expected 'P2' — customer is pro plan with status past_due, model assigned P3
triage/policy.py line: 'P2: production outage for a pro customer, any issue for an enterprise customer, or a past_due account that cannot pay.'
triage/prompts.py current P2 rule does not mention past_due accounts at all
round 2 rejection note: 'no measurable improvement' — the diff added the rule but the wording was awkward and may not have been clear enough to the model
hypothesis.fix_plan: Update the P2 bullet in SYSTEM to exactly mirror policy.py: add 'OR any customer with a past_due account status' as a clean third condition. Also update P3 to explicitly exclude past_due accounts so the model doesn't fall back to P3 for billing/account issues on past_due accounts. The key difference from round 2 is cleaner, more direct language that matches policy.py exactly.
hypothesis.expected_effect: The past-due task should flip from failed to passed (priority P3→P2). No other tasks should be affected since they are already passing. Net: 1 more task passes, pass_rate goes from 0.833 to 1.0.
